Minnesota law sets out when a person occupying land can claim title by adverse possession, and how an owner can remove someone who has no right to be there.

What the official sources say

  • No action to recover real estate may be maintained unless plaintiff or predecessor was seized or possessed of the premises within 15 years before the action (15-year limitation). (Minn. Stat. 541.02; source)
  • For separately assessed parcels, the limitation does not bar the action unless the adverse claimant (or predecessors) paid taxes on the land at least five consecutive years of the claimed occupancy. (Minn. Stat. 541.02 para. 2; source)
  • The tax-payment requirement does not apply to boundary-line actions established by adverse possession or to lands not assessed for taxation. (Minn. Stat. 541.02 para. 3; source)
  • A person who holds over after the redemption period on a mortgage foreclosure, execution sale or tax judgment sale, or holds over after lease termination or after tenancy-at-will notice to quit, may be removed by an eviction action. (Minn. Stat. 504B.285 subd. 1(a); source)

Last updated November 14, 2026.

Minnesota statutes set the basic rules between landlords and tenants, including deposits, notices and what happens when a rental is sold.

What the official sources say

  • Landlord must return the deposit with interest, or give a written statement of specific reasons for withholding, within three weeks after termination of tenancy (five days if tenant leaves due to legal condemnation), after receiving tenant's mailing address. (Minn. Stat. 504B.178 subd. 3; source)
  • On termination of the landlord's interest (sale, etc.) the landlord must within 60 days transfer the deposit (with interest) to the successor and notify the tenant, or return it to the tenant; the successor assumes the landlord's deposit obligations. (Minn. Stat. 504B.178 subds. 5-6; source)
  • A tenant may not withhold last month's rent on the ground that the deposit should serve as payment. (Minn. Stat. 504B.178 subd. 8; source)
  • Tenancy at will: written notice at least as long as the rent interval or three months, whichever is less. (Minn. Stat. 504B.135; source)
  • Landlord entry requires a reasonable business purpose and good-faith effort at reasonable notice of not less than 24 hours, between 8:00 a.m. and 8:00 p.m. unless agreed; showing the unit to a prospective buyer is a reasonable purpose; penalty up to $500 civil penalty per violation plus fees. (Minn. Stat. 504B.211 subds. 2, 3, 6; source)
  • Landlord covenants fitness, reasonable repair, compliance with health and safety laws, pest extermination and 68F heat Oct 1-Apr 30; covenants cannot be waived or modified. (Minn. Stat. 504B.161 subd. 1; source)
  • Tenant may not be evicted or have obligations increased/services decreased as a penalty for a complaint of a violation; landlord bears the burden within 90 days of the complaint. (Minn. Stat. 504B.441; source)

Last updated November 14, 2026.

Minnesota law requires a landlord to give a specific written notice before filing an eviction, and the number of days depends on the reason.

What the official sources say

  • Before an eviction for nonpayment, landlord must give written notice (total due, accounting, required statements) stating the tenant may be sued if not paid or moved out within 14 days; local rules may require longer. (Minn. Stat. 504B.321 subd. 1a; source)
  • The nonpayment notice must be delivered personally or by first class mail to the tenant at the leased premises. (Minn. Stat. 504B.321 subd. 1a(b); source)
  • An eviction action starts by filing a complaint with the court, with a copy of the written notice attached. (Minn. Stat. 504B.321 subd. 1; source)
  • Eviction lies when a tenant holds over after lease term expires or contrary to lease conditions, or a tenant at will holds over after notice to quit. (Minn. Stat. 504B.285 subd. 1(a)(2)-(3); source)
  • Tenant at will must be given written termination notice at least as long as the rent interval or three months, whichever is less. (Minn. Stat. 504B.135; source)
